$comment: Questions manifest for the project-context injection flow. Data, not prose: the `project-context` agent and `update-project-context` skill READ this to know what to ask; `register-context` WRITES to it when a new capability needs init-time context. Never hand-edit the generated .claude/.cursor files to change interview behaviour — change this manifest. This file is NOT consumed by ai-build.mjs (it only reads ai/shared + ai/capabilities), so it never affects the drift gate.

purpose.note: The repo's purpose paragraph. Written under the '# cube' heading, replacing the 'generated from the company skeleton' boilerplate intro is NOT allowed — append a 'What this repo is for' paragraph instead so the standards intro survives.

features.note: The service description paragraph and the feature-map list. Replaces the FILL-IN placeholder blocks.

rules.note: Repo-specific rules that are NOT house standards (those live in 10-conventions.md and the stack files). Appended as bullet points under the existing headings.

seed.prompt: In one short paragraph: what is this service/repo for, and who uses it? (Agents read this to understand intent, not just code.)
Describe what this service does in 2-4 sentences for the '# What this service does' section.
List the current features/domains, one per line, as 'feature — one-line purpose — key entry points (paths)'. Leave blank if there are none yet.
Any product ideas, roadmap intent, or 'north star' context that should guide agents working here? (Optional — kept as a short 'Direction' note.)

Any repo-SPECIFIC rules that are NOT already house standards? (e.g. 'all money is stored in minor units', 'never call the legacy /v1 API', domain invariants). One per line. House-wide conventions do NOT belong here.
